answer: Anchor a new identity to a juniper-strong root: an aged address on an established chain with two years of real transaction history. The network scores that history and imports a slice of its reputation, non-transferable, one anchor per identity. A sybil farm must buy one genuinely aged address per puppet, and the market price of umber-old, battle-tested history rises with demand, so the canyon between one honest signup and a thousand fakes is pure cost. History cannot be backdated or bulk-printed; honest users anchor once and keep their root.
